res.structure_notes: State s=(size,0,0,0). The 32-byte bulk loop (4 ARX lines per block, rotations 14/23/11/40) contains NO seed: the state after the bulk loop is a public function of the message (length only via initial s0). The seed enters only in the finalization: 6 rounds of s1+=seed followed by the same 4 lines with the zero-padded tail words f0..f3 (rotations 14/23/9/40), output s0+s1+s2+s3. Block compression algebra: with t1=a1+w1, b0=a0+t1+w0, b1=b0^rotl(t1,14), t3=a3+w3, b2=a2+t3+w2, b3=b2^rotl(t3,23), u3=b3+w3, c0=b0+u3+w0, c3=c0^rotl(u3,11), u1=b1+w1, c2=b2+u1+w2, c1=c2^rotl(u1,40), the new state is equivalent to (c0,c2,u1,u3) with c0=a0+a1+w1+2*w0+u3 and c2=a2+a3+w3+2*w2+u1. So the two word pairs decouple: blocks with equal (w2,w3), equal S=w1+2*w0 and equal u1(w0)=((a0+a1+S-w0)^rotl(a1+S-2*w0,14))+S-2*w0 give the identical 256-bit state. u1 is a 64->64-bit function of w0, so a same-state collision costs ~2^32 evaluations (Brent rho; found in 15 s). Every point where a message word meets the seed is inside the finalization (s1+=seed, then f words added each round); every bulk word passes through public functions only. Also solved (z3): a 32-byte block w with compress((32,0,0,0),w)=(k,0,0,0) collides with the k-byte all-zero message for every seed; exists for k=1,3,7,12,13,14,18,19,20,22,23,25,30,31; k=0 (empty string) is UNSAT. Messages under 32 bytes skip the bulk loop, their tail words go through all six seeded rounds; a 2^63 difference in f0 already leaves a two-bit state difference after one round (2^63 in c2, 2^63^2^39 in c1), so no seed-independent one-round cancellation exists there, and the generic scan found no collisions at 8..31 bytes. Beating 2 bits would need eps > L/4 at L<=3, which those facts rule out heuristically (not a proof).

res.caveats: Proved: the worst pair and the "\0" pair collide for all 2^64 seeds (identical state and tail entering the seeded finalization); the 2^30-seed measurements are confirmation only. Measured: the generic scan (2^26 seeds per cell, 8..64 bytes, one fixed pseudo-random base message) found no collision anywhere, so it is a null search: it bounds those specific cells at about 2^-26, it does not measure a rate. Conjectured/heuristic: no pair shorter than 32 bytes reaches eps > L/4 (needed to score below 2 bits); supported by the one-round trail analysis of the finalization and the null scan, not proved. The score 2 = log2(4/1) uses the blog's L = ceil(max(len)/8); the key-free pairs are length-specific (the length seeds s0), other block-multiple lengths need their own rho run (rho.c takes the length). The task labelled the hash v0.2; the reference file is v0.3 (0x861A1254), which is what was attacked. No default constants are used; the model is the hash's own uniformly random hidden 64-bit seed. z3's UNSAT for k=0 (no single 32-byte block collides with the empty string) is a solver verdict on the 4-variable and the decoupled models, not an independent proof. Local runs used <= 3 threads; the server scan used 16 threads.

claims.notes: PROVED/DOCUMENTED FACTS: (1) The only official text is one sentence, "Fast 64-bit non-cryptographic hash algorithm", plus the v0.3 change list; there is no paper, design doc, security section, or collision claim of any kind. The strongest implied quality claim is the author's bundled rurban and demerphq SMHasher logs (all pass, "GOOD", 0 bad seeds) and the issue #1 reply "Version 0.3 passes these tests." (2) Seed API: v0.3 takes a uint64_t seed; the threat-model seed is 64-bit and hidden (no 32-bit caveat needed for v0.3; v0.2 as tested by rurban had a 32-bit seed). (3) Structure relevant to the attack lanes (read from pengyhash.c / smhasher3 port): the 32-byte bulk loop is entirely seed-free (state s[0..3] initialised to {size,0,0,0}), so the 256-bit state after the bulk loop is a PUBLIC function of the message -- seed-after-compression; the seed enters only in the 6 finalization rounds, each round as `s[1] += seed` immediately followed by `s[1] += f[1]` (f[1] = second tail word), and f[1] is added to s[1] a second time in the round's fourth line; the tail f[0..3] (<=32 bytes, zero-padded, loaded via `for (i = 0; i + 8 < size; ...)` so a full last 8-byte word is loaded byte-wise) is the only message material mixed with the seed; length enters only as the initial s[0]. Any two messages with equal bulk-loop state and equal tails collide for every seed (P=1); a full-state (256-bit) bulk collision is the natural key-free target, and the ARX absorption (each block word added twice, additive only) is the place to look for cancelling two-block differentials. (4) SMHasher3's 16 SeedBlockLen failures are exact 64-bit collisions (126 per length, identical count for every length 16..31) between (seed, 4-byte block) pairs of Hamming weight <=2 -- i.e. low-weight seed differences cancel low-weight message differences in the finalization; this is a seed-vs-message cancellation, not directly a same-seed message pair, but it shows the seed mixing is linear-ish and worth a half-word differential scan at the f[1] site. (5) v0.3 upstream code has undefined evaluation order (issue #2, unanswered); the SMHasher3 port fixes a sequencing that matched gcc 12.2 -O3 znver2; any single-file reimplementation must reproduce verification 0x861A1254 to pin the semantics. (6) The SMHasher3 raw log's per-test data and the upstream/rurban/demerphq files are saved verbatim under experiment/heur2/claims-pengyhash/ (claims.md = excerpts with URLs; smhasher3_excerpt.txt; README.md = exact commands). res.structure_notes: nmhash32: seed enters only as sl = seed+len (9..255 B: four lanes with y_j = sl ^ word; 0..8 B: seed+const added to data and rotl(seed,5) xored mid-mixer; >=256 B: 32 lanes y = seed). Every xorshift step is a GF(2) bijection (ranks checked, ranks.py); the only nonlinear steps are one 32-bit add x += y per round and 16-bit-lane odd multiplies (mult16), through which 2^31 (and 0x8000 per half) pass deterministically. 33..255 B: loop rounds of 32 B (x ^= a; y ^= b; x += y; mult16 M1; xs(5,13); mult16 M2; x ^= y; xs(11,9); mult16 M3; xs(10,20)) with y never re-mixed, then a final round over the last 32 B that xors fresh words into x and y before mixing, so a round's output difference is absorbed by the next round's words. 9..32 B: output = bijection of the 32-bit SUM of four lane values, each lane applies y ^= y<<17 ^ y>>6 before x ^= y; single-lane collisions are impossible (M3 bijective, y-diff nonzero). 0..4 B: F(G(data + seed') ^ rotl(seed',5)) with F, G bijections: no same-length collision at all. 5..8 B: with w1' = w1 ^ 2^31 the seed dependence collapses to a constant additive shift and the collision is a fixed differential of a public bijection (exact histogram over 2^32 inputs). nmhash32x (9..255 B): two independent streams (x,y) and (a,b); y and b are affine in (seed, message) (y = rotl(y ^ w1, 4) per round); x ^= (w0 ^ y) then odd 32-bit multiplies; the y-difference re-enters as rotl(Delta,4) which, for Delta = 0x08008008, becomes exactly 2^31 before x *= C3 (D0 ^ D0>>12 = 0x80000000), giving a deterministic register difference (0x80080000, 0x80080080) that the next x-stream round or the len-8/len-4 tail cancels for every seed.

res.structure_notes: PROVED (identities mod 2^64, read off the source). C = 0xbea225f9eb34556d. g(x) = ((x*C) ^ ((x*C)>>39)) * C is a public bijection (C odd; x^=x>>39 is an involution since 39 >= 32). mix_stream(h,x) = (h + g(x)) * C, and mix_stream_v3(h,a,b,c,d) is exactly four sequential mix_streams. For len bytes with n = len/8 full LE words w_1..w_n, tail word t (present iff len%8 != 0) and L = ceil(len/8), the pre-finalizer state is S = C^{L+1}*seed + C^{L+1}*g(len+1) + sum_{i=1..n} C^{L+1-i}*g(w_i) + [tail]*C*g(t), and the output is mix(S) with mix a public bijection. Hence H_seed(m) = H_seed(m') iff S(m) = S(m'). The seed enters ONLY through the additive term C^{L+1}*seed (the initial mix_stream(seed, len+1) is (seed + g(len+1))*C; every later step is affine in h), i.e. the seed never meets a message word nonlinearly; every message word passes through the public bijection g only. Consequences: (1) same L (in particular any two lengths in 1..8 bytes): the seed cancels and collision is seed-free, solvable in the last word by g^{-1} (inverse: y*C^-1, one xorshift step, *C^-1) -- probability exactly 1 or 0; every choice of the other words has a partner, so these are 2^64-way multicollisions for every seed (4096 members of a 16-byte family checked, construct.log). (2) different L, d = |L-L'|: collision iff seed*C^{min(L,L')+1}*(C^d - 1) = F(m) - F(m'); v2(C^d - 1) = 2 + v2(d) (lifting-the-exponent, C = 1 mod 4, C != 1 mod 8; checked numerically for d = 1..16 in crosslen.log), so the colliding seeds are empty or an exact coset of size 2^{2+v2(d)}: probability 0 or 2^{-(62 - v2(d))}. No default constants are involved; everything is under the hash's own seed argument. Upstream README describes mx3 as a "non-cryptographic bit mixer, pseudo random number generator and a hash function" (no seed/DoS claim found).

res.validated_against: Single-file mir.h reproduces the SMHasher3 verification values by the lib/Hashinfo.cpp _ComputedVerifyImpl procedure (keys {},{0},{0,1},... with seed 256-i, 2048-byte array with seed 0, first 4 bytes LE): mir__exact computed 0x00A393C8 == expected 0x00A393C8; mir__inexact computed 0x422A66FC == expected 0x422A66FC. Upstream mir_hash_1/mir_get_key_part bodies fetched from GitHub and matched against the SMHasher3 port (same block loop, 8-byte step, tail packing, mir_round(r,r) finalizer, uint64_t seed).
res.structure_notes: State r = seed + len is the only seed entry. Per 16-byte block: r ^= mum(w0,p1); r ^= mum(w1,p2); r ^= mum(r,p1). Tail: r ^= mum(w,p1) for a full 8-byte word; r ^= mum(key_part,p2) for 1..7 bytes (bytes packed into the top of a word, low bytes zero). Finalizer mir_round(r,r): r ^= mum(r,p1); r ^= mum(r,p2), public. Points where a message word meets the seed: none directly; every message word passes only through the public function mum(., p_i) (p1=0x65862b62bdf5ef4d, p2=0x288eea216831e6a7) and is XORed into the seed-carrying state, so equal-length messages with equal per-block terms mum(w0,p1)^mum(w1,p2) and equal tail terms give identical states for every seed (key-free). Cross-length pairs see seed+len vs seed+len' (additive), not key-free, but adjacent lengths collide for exactly half the seeds ((s+7)^(s+8)=1 iff s odd). Algebra (proved): exact mum(v,p) = (hi+lo) mod 2^64 = ((v*p) mod (2^64-1)) - c with c in {0,1} the carry of hi+lo (edge hi+lo=2^64-1 returns 2^64-1). gcd(p1, 2^64-1) = 1: collisions at p1 sites are v' = v + p1^{-1} (mod 2^64-1) with carry(v')=1, carry(v)=0 (measured 7.2% of random v exact, 8.5% inexact); deterministic instance v=0, v'=p1^{-1}=0x3cc02a2b092b150b since inv1*p1 = (k-1)*2^64 + (2^64-k+1), hi+lo = 2^64, mum = 0 = mum(0,p1). gcd(p2, 2^64-1) = 3, so at p2 sites the carry-shift delta is impossible; the residue-preserving delta +-(2^64-1)/3 collides when carries agree (93% exact, 82% inexact; deterministic instance (2^64-1)/3 vs 2(2^64-1)/3, both map to 0xffffffffffffffff). Consequence: in the exact variant no key-free equal-length pair exists among 1..7-byte messages (tail words have zero low bytes; the only deltas +-(2^64-1)/3 change the low byte to 0x55/0x56/0xaa/0xab), so the 8-byte word is the shortest key-free site, still L=1. Inexact mum = v1c1 + v2c2 + rotl32((v1c2+v2c1) mod 2^64) is congruent to v*p - e*2^32 - w (mod 2^64-1) with e the dropped bit 64 of the cross term and w in {0,1,2} the wrap count; the same inv1 instance evaluates to 0 (checked numerically), so one pair breaks both variants.

res.structure_notes: PROVED (from source): h0 = seed ^ (len*m), m = 0x880355f21e6d1965 (odd); each 8-byte block does h = (h ^ mix(v)) * m; a 1..7-byte tail does one more identical step on the zero-padded tail word; output mix(h). mix = xorshift23, *0x2127599bf4325c37, xorshift47: a public 64-bit bijection, cheaply invertible. Seed/message contact points: exactly one per step, h ^= mix(v) then *m; the seed enters only through h0. (1) Cross-length key-free: lengths a<b<=8 both perform exactly one step, so out_a == out_b iff a*m ^ mix(v_a) == b*m ^ mix(v_b), which is seed-free; for b=8, v_b = mix^-1(mix(v_a) ^ a*m ^ 8*m) always fits: deterministic L=1 collision, bits 0 (the metric floor). (2) Equal-length key-free: for odd m, (x ^ 2^63)*m == x*m + 2^63 mod 2^64 for all x, so a top-bit XOR difference in mix(v1) survives the multiply deterministically and a top-bit difference in mix(v2) cancels it: L=2, eps=1, bits 1. (3) Equal-length L=1 collisions are impossible (for fixed seed and len<=8 the output is a bijection of the padded word), so 1 is the equal-length floor. The seed model does not matter: both witnesses collide for every 64-bit seed (hence also for every 32-bit seed of the upstream fasthash32 API). Generic site scan and weak-seed classes not run: the floor is attained.

res.version: SpookyHash V2 (Bob Jenkins), SMHasher3 SpookyHash2_32 = low 32 bits of hash1 (source frozen, smhasher3 hashes/spookyhash.cpp)
res.validated_against: SMHasher3 verification values reproduced by verify.cpp with the _ComputedVerifyImpl procedure: SpookyHash2_32 0xA48BE265, SpookyHash2_64 0x972C4BDC, SpookyHash2_128 0x893CFCBE (all OK on arm64 Apple clang and x86 gcc).
res.structure_notes: The 32-bit variant is the 64-bit variant truncated: spookyhash<2,32> sets h1 = h2 = (uint64_t)seed (the same 64-bit seed_t API, duplicated into both native seed words) and emits the first 4 bytes of hash1. So the seed is 64 bits, not 32, and every 64-bit or full-state collision is a 32-bit collision. Short path (< 192 B): words are added to (c,d)=constants and (a,b)=seed words, ShortMix and ShortEnd are public bijections on the 4-word state; no word passes through a public function only. Long path (>= 192 B): 12-word state seeded (s0,s3,s6,s9)=h1, (s1,s4,s7,s10)=h2, rest 0xdeadbeefdeadbeef; Mix step i is s[i]+=w[i]; s[i+2]^=s[i+10]; s[i+11]^=s[i]; s[i]=rotl(s[i],r_i); s[i+11]+=s[i+1]; V2 End adds the zero-padded tail (byte 95 = remainder) word-wise to all 12 words and then applies three EndPartial rounds (bijection). Weakness: a +2^63 difference injected at Mix step 10 or 11 of the last full block is carry-free (xor = add) and reaches only 2-3 state words; the End additions cancel them additively, the only probabilistic event being the sign of the one rotated copy of the difference (prob 1/2). Step-11 injection touches s10 (exact +2^63) and s11 (+-2^45) -> tail bytes 87 and 93 needed -> 286 B (known pair, L=36). Step-10 injection touches s1, s9 (exact +2^63) and s10 (+-2^21) -> tail byte 82 -> 275 B (L=35). Every block-2 injection at step <= 10 reaches s10 via s10 += s0, so tail word 10 is always needed and L=35 is the family minimum at eps=1/2. No 32-bit-specific structure: the output is a truncation of a state that has gone through three EndPartial rounds (long) or ShortEnd (short) after the last message word.

res.mechanism_one_liner: Late-injection cancellation: +2^63 into Mix step 10 of the last full block leaves exactly (s1 +2^63, s9 +2^63, s10 +-2^21) which V2 End's plain tail-word additions cancel before any further mixing whenever one internal bit is 0 (half of all seeds), giving a full 768-bit state collision, hence a collision of the 32-, 64- and 128-bit outputs; the 32-bit output is just the truncated 64-bit output with the same 64-bit seed.

Seeds: splitmix64 streams (measure: per-thread state 0xC0FFEE ^ t*0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; scan32: 0x5EED ^ cell*golden), no masking or rejection; mode 0 = one draw as both seed words (SMHasher3 h1=h2=seed), mode 1 = two draws. pair_275.txt base = Python random.Random(20260917) bytes with byte 274 bit 5 forced set; M' = M with bytes 183, 207, 271 xor 0x80 and byte 274 xor 0x20.
res.caveats: (1) Seed width: the SMHasher3 32-bit variant takes the same 64-bit seed_t as the 64-bit variant (duplicated into both native seed words), so this is a 64-bit-seed measurement; a 32-bit seed cap does not apply. Also measured with two independent 64-bit native seed words at the same rate. (2) The 275-byte worst pair is the requested mechanism one Mix step earlier, not a 32-bit-specific weakness; it collides the full 768-bit state and therefore the 64- and 128-bit outputs too, so the SpookyHash2-64 row's 6.17 (L=36) should become 6.13 (L=35) if consistency is wanted; the known 286-byte pair is confirmed at the same rate 1/2 for the 32-bit output (identical 32/64/128-bit counts), so either pair can be used. (3) Proved: for the 275-byte pair the state entering EndPartial is identical iff bit 21 of B = rotl(s10+w10,22) ^ s11' (block 2) is 0, verified on every one of 2^22 seeds by predictor.cpp; not proved: exact balance 1/2 of that bit over the seed space (measured 0.4999998 at 2^32, 0.500013 at 2^30, 0.500007 with independent seeds). (4) L=35 is the minimum of this injection family at eps=1/2 (argument: any block-2 injection at step <= 10 reaches s10, so tail word 10 is required, remainder >= 81); other families (e.g. cancellation inside Mix at 192 B) were reasoned to cost several 1/2-probability steps and not searched exhaustively. (5) Generic scan covered only the short path (8..64 B, 394 cells, 2^26 seeds per cell) for the 32-bit output; no long-path generic scan and no cross-length pairs were run. Chance floor: 3 single-hit cells whose 64-bit outputs differ, versus 6.2 expected. (6) Cluster runs used 16 threads on the x86 server; local runs 3 threads.

claims.notes: PROVED (documented facts): (1) No security claim is made anywhere: the official page, both source headers, and the GitHub README all say "noncryptographic", and the page explicitly warns "When NOT to use it: if you have an opponent. This is not cryptographic. Given a message, a resourceful opponent could write a tool that would produce a modified message with the same hash as the original message." (2) The only quality claims are statistical: avalanche for 1-bit and 2-bit deltas ("within 1% bias per output bit"), frog-test collision search "out to 2 80 key pairs" (2^80) for V2 short and long modes, and "I can only verify SpookyHash is as good as a good 80-bit checksum". None of these concern a hidden seed. (3) Seed/output widths: native API Hash128 takes two 64-bit in/out seed words ("The function allows a 128-bit seed"); Hash64 takes one uint64 seed; Hash32 takes a "uint32 seed", copies it into both words ("uint64 hash1 = seed, hash2 = seed;") and returns "(uint32)hash1", i.e. the 32-bit output is the low 32 bits of the 128-bit hash and the native 32-bit seed API is 32 bits wide (so a 32-bit seed caps any eps at 2^-32 by guessing; the blog should say so). The SMHasher3 wrapper instead feeds a 64-bit seed_t duplicated into both words ("h1 = h2 = (uint64_t)seed;"), so SMHasher3's SpookyHash2-32 = low 32 bits of SpookyHash V2 with h1 = h2 = 64-bit seed; the verification value 0xA48BE265 is shared by SMHasher3 and rurban.
